images.title: Count first, then tile
images.purpose: Recap the topic's method: count the squares; an odd count means no tiling, and an even side lets the tiles line up.
images.composition: One short heading at the top centre with two grey arrows branching down to two small grids, left and right, with wide white space between them.
exact_structure: Top centre: the heading count the squares, with 2 grey (#6B7280) arrows going down, one to the left and one to the right.

Left: a grid of 3 rows and 3 columns (9 squares) labelled 3 × 3 above, with exactly 4 tiles of 2 × 1 arranged in a pinwheel round the centre, filled teal (#0072B2), and the centre square left uncovered and filled vermilion (#D55E00); a vermilion (#D55E00) cross beneath; caption 9 is odd.

Right: a grid of 2 rows and 5 columns (10 squares) labelled 2 × 5 above, fully covered by exactly 5 vertical tiles filled green (#009E73) with thick dark outlines; a green (#009E73) tick beneath; caption 10 is even.
rejection: the left grid with more or fewer than 4 tiles or without the uncovered centre square
the right grid not fully covered by exactly 5 vertical tiles
a tick under the 3 × 3 grid or a cross under the 2 × 5 grid
images.takeaway: Count the squares first: an odd count can never be tiled, and an even side lets tiles fill every column or row.
images.description: A heading, count the squares, branches to a 3 by 3 grid with one square left over and a 2 by 5 grid fully tiled with 5 vertical tiles.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept on tiling grids or proving it impossible, before the student uses the domino grid tool.
images.teaching_notes: Have students check the count before placing any tile, then use the even side to choose vertical or horizontal tiles.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap shows the topic's method: count first, then use the even side.
